In what circumstances might you be able not just forgive someone who has made that minor, yet potentially costly or impactful error?

As we gathered to start another meeting, my heart thumping nervingly with each second ticking, there stood in stark contrast a person whose casual tone belched an eerie confidence and assurance. She breezzily introduced me and another colleague in an almost mocking manner before proceeding as we had planned for an interlude.

I stood, feeling exposed as a deer trapped within headlights. The embarrassment gnashed away like acid on my self-image, my confidence evaporating with my self-composed facade of poising comely. In those brief, frozen few breathless heart-stopped instants where all that was expected to happen happened at the exact instant that was not at, a minor but crucial slip of my memory came forth and was revealed to everyone, my boss, colleagues. In the face, I was not a competent individual who was well-qualified to lead. The moment I had prepared so diligently was tarnishing with an ugly stain, as the meeting started with a bang and an almost deafly silent hushing.

As if the moment were still not quite real
